mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%, indicating the labor market signal is not reliably bearish.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly negative in periods following a sharp INDPRO deceleration (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month change > 10%) and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a housing boom that will boost cyclical sectors and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts growth reverts to negative territory within 6 months of the signal, indicating the boom was short-lived and not supportive of sustained equity gains.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the consumer price index (CPI) above 3% signals an inflation scare that will prompt the Fed to aggressively raise rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed does not raise rates by at least 50 bps within 3 months of the CPI signal, indicating the inflation scare was transitory and did not warrant a significant policy response.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -100k) and the unemployment rate is already above 6%, it signals a looming recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The economy avoids a recession (defined as 2+ consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth) within 12 months of the signal, indicating the labor market weakness was not a reliable recession indicator.

mechanism_narrative: Real estate investment trust (REIT) prices, as measured by the FTSE NAREIT All Equity REITs index, tend to lead the broader stock market. When REITs outperform the S&P 500 by more than 5% over the past 3 months, it signals a coming rally in cyclical sectors that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: REITs underperform the S&P 500 over the subsequent 20 trading days in > 60% of instances where they outperformed by > 5% in the prior 3 months, indicating the REIT signal is not a reliable leading indicator.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM manufacturing PMI falls below 45, indicating a sharp contraction in factory activity, it signals an impending recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if the PMI remains below 45 for 2+ consecutive months.
failure_condition: The ISM PMI rebounds above 50 within 3 months of falling below 45, indicating the manufacturing contraction was short-lived and did not presage a broader economic downturn.
